newsitem.title: SPAIN: Santander buys majority in Argentine bank.
newsitem.headline: Santander buys majority in Argentine bank.

text.p: Spain's Banco Santander said on Tuesday it would take control of Argentine Banco Rio de la Plata, S.A. with 51 percent of the voting rights, acquiring 35.06 percent of its share capital and an option for an additional 15 percent.

In a statement detailing a deal announced earlier today, Santander said: "The operation will involve payment of $594 million by Banco Santander, and the transfer to Sudacia, S.A., 100 percent owned by the Perez Companc family, of approximately six percent of Banco Santander Chile."
Gregorio Perez Companc is the main shareholder in Banco Rio de la Plata.
The agreement foresees a merger between Banco Rio and Banco Santander Argentina, creating the largest private bank in the country, with assets in excess of $10 billion.

"...Rio de la Plata, is in our opinion, the best banking franchise in the country with a magnificent tradition, financial strength, and excellent banking operations," Santander Chairman Emilio Botin said.
"It is an agreement that fits perfectly with our retail banking strategy in Latin America and strengthens our presence as the leader in wholesale and pension funds in Argentina," he said.

Banco Rio has a $4.82 billion loan portfolio, giving it market share of 6.9 percent. It has the lowest non-performing loan ratio among Argentine banks, standing at 3.04 percent with a provision coverage rate of 105 percent.
Banco Rio has deposits totalling $3.59 billion, for a 6.2 percent market share.
In the last fiscal year ended June 1996, Banco Rio had net profit of $90.3 million.
The investment will cease to be dilutive from the second year, in line with profitability goals recently announced by Banco Santander, the statement said.
